records.name: PILLARC Foundation
records.summary: A foundation that works on mental health awareness, drug and addiction prevention, and violence prevention. It says its work is rooted in Philadelphia, Manhattan and the Bronx, and its site describes workshops and forums but lists no dates.
records.what_you_do: Attend a workshop or forum, or ask how to join a youth program or school outreach effort. The site lists no dates.

first_step.how: Email info@pillarc.org to ask about upcoming workshops, forums and youth programs in Philadelphia. The site also lists a phone number for questions.
first_step.basis: The site gives an email and a phone number, but it lists no dated events, no sign-up pages and no program details.

records.notes: Thin site. The three focus-area links on the services page go to an unrelated theme demo site, and the only action offered is Donate Now. No workshop, forum or youth program has a date, a sign-up step or a description of who may attend. The tap-to-call links use +1-236-789-4563, which differs from the printed number; the printed number is used here. The contact page lists New York, Philadelphia PA and Nigeria (Kogi and Abuja), and does not name a Philadelphia office. The about page names Nelson Abdul as founder and Mercy A as project manager; the contact name Michael Abdul comes only from IRS and NCCS data and was not seen on the site. A second email, pillarc2023@gmail.com, is listed under the Nigeria section and was not recorded. The one search found no PILLARC event pages. The gallery has five undated photos. Owner review recommended before this stays live.

records.name: Socks for the Streets
records.summary: Gives socks, hygiene items, clothing and snacks to people facing homelessness or addiction, and helps connect them to shelters, treatment and other services. Most people take part by donating, and the group began with a sock drive.
records.what_you_do: Donate socks, hygiene items, food, clothing or money. Volunteers help at the group's resource fairs, giveaways and other events; to ask about shifts, fill in the contact form on the website.

first_step.how: Fill in the contact form on socksforthestreets.org to ask about volunteer opportunities. The form asks for your name, email and a message.
first_step.basis: A public form invites people to ask about volunteering, but the site names no shifts, roles, training or age limits.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a resource fair and family fun day listed for Saturday, September 19, 2026 on the news page. That page embeds Facebook posts, so the month rests on the event listing shown there. The contact page says the group provides community service hours but describes no letter, so service_hours_letter stays unknown. No drop-off address or hours are published. Partner organizations named on the what-we-do page are listed under leads_only; their own websites were not found.

records.name: Torresdale Boys Club
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia club with baseball, softball, soccer, and basketball teams for boys and girls, with in-house and travel teams sorted by age.
records.what_you_do: Kids join in-house or travel teams by age and can take part in neighborhood social and community service events. Parents are encouraged to volunteer as coaches. Current updates are sent to a Facebook group.

schedule.text: Teams practice about once a week and play games mostly on Saturdays, with Friday night games for some boys' basketball teams. Seasons differ by sport: soccer starts in September, basketball runs from mid-November to mid-March, and in-house baseball starts after Easter.

cost.text: Soccer and in-house baseball are $80 per child. Soccer and baseball travel teams cost $165 for the first child and $125 for each more. Basketball is $90 for Little Hoopers and $150 for Developmental, with travel at $165. The family cap is $325. Scholarship help is not stated.

first_step.how: Sign your child up online during a sport's registration window. The soccer page gives April 1 to June 30, and the baseball page says registration is closed for 2026. Travel teams also need a copy of the child's birth certificate and a headshot.
first_step.basis: Sign-up is online and open to any family during a set window, and the club says travel teams can fill or hold tryouts; the basketball page does not say how to sign up.

records.what_to_expect: Kids practice about once a week and play games mostly on Saturdays. In-house teams are recreational, and travel teams play in city or suburban leagues, where some children may be cut if there is no room.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own glove for in-house baseball.
For travel teams, have a copy of your child's birth certificate and a headshot ready for the coach.
Baseball players must also register with the Phillies JR RBI league, and the club says it will post that link later.
records.notes: The 2026 date comes from the baseball page: its ages are counted as of May 1, 2026 and its registration heading says closed for 2026. The month is taken from that May 1 date, not from a registration event. The soccer page's sign-up window reads Fall 2025 and no year is attached to its April and June dates. The club's gym address is not stated on the pages read, so the only location is the IRS mailing address. Practice times are not given for basketball, baseball or softball. Volunteer coaches' names and phone numbers appear on the sport pages and were left out on purpose; the club website and its Facebook group are the way in. The Facebook group link comes from the club's own site and was not read. The youngest in-house programs are for ages 3 and 4, which sets min_age.

records.name: Charlie's Army Animal Rescue
records.summary: A small Philadelphia rescue that takes in stray and abandoned cats and kittens, gets them medical care, and finds them homes. It depends on foster homes, adopters and donors.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat or kitten at home until it is adopted, or drive animals to clinics and vet visits if you have a vehicle. You can also donate or apply to adopt a cat that is listed as available.

cost.text: The site does not state an adoption fee or donation amounts. For foster parents, the rescue covers medical costs and can provide supplies.

first_step.how: Start the application for the role you want on the website: charliesarmy.com/foster for fostering, charliesarmy.com/transport for driving, or charliesarmy.com/apply to adopt a cat listed as available.
first_step.basis: Fostering, transport and adoption each start with a written application, the site says approval is not guaranteed, and it does not give a review time.

records.what_to_expect: Fosters keep a cat or kitten until it is adopted, and they set aside an easy-to-clean space to keep new arrivals apart for three weeks. The rescue covers medical costs and can supply items, and foster parents can ask the rescue president for guidance. Transport drivers take small groups of animals to clinics, with a drop-off typically around 8:30 am and a pick-up by 4 pm.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the application fully and honestly, since the rescue treats it as your first impression of them.
For fostering, keep a room or playpen that is easy to clean ready for a three-week quarantine.
Email info@charliesarmy.com with questions before you apply.
records.notes: The adoption fee, donation amounts and volunteer requirements (age, vehicle, home visit) are not stated, so none are recorded. The apply page covers adoption only. The IRS address on file includes an apartment number and may be a private home; the site gives no visiting place. The owner should decide whether to keep it published. The transport page names several veterinary hospitals and the city's ACCT shelter as places animals go or come from. The hospitals are businesses and were not recorded; ACCT is listed under leads_only.

records.name: Friends of Bodine
records.summary: A friends group that supports Bodine school and its students through community socials and fundraising. People can keep up with events through a mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Come to the socials, RSVP through the site, or sign up for the mailing list to hear about the next event.

schedule.text: Socials are held as one-off events and announced one at a time on the events page.

first_step.how: Use the RSVP HERE link on the events page to RSVP for the 2026 fall social, and sign up for the mailing list to hear about the next event.
first_step.basis: Socials are posted publicly with an RSVP form and a mailing list sign-up, but the site does not say whether they are members only.

records.what_to_expect: The listed 2026 fall social is at a Philadelphia brewery, and you RSVP through the form on the events page. The site does not say how long a social lasts, who attends, or what it costs.
records.notes: The events page lists a 2026 fall social with no day or month, so last_sign_of_life is left out rather than guessing a month; the 2026 date is used only for status and the RSVP step. The Meet the Board page says the group supports Bodine, a Philadelphia school, so the category moved from civic association to school parent groups. Nothing on the site says who may attend socials, so open to public is carried over from tier 1 and is not confirmed. The RSVP link is a Google form and was not opened. The about page returned 404.

records.name: Sergio Foundation
records.summary: A charity that gathers clothing, food and toiletries and hands them out to people who are homeless or going through hard times. Volunteers help serve warm meals and pack toiletry bags.
records.what_you_do: Serve warm meals or pack toiletry bags as a volunteer, or donate items or money.

first_step.how: Fill in the Get involved form on the Contact Us page of sergiofoundation.com to ask about volunteer opportunities. It asks for your name, email and where you heard about the group.
first_step.basis: A public Get involved form invites anyone to ask about volunteering, but the site names no shifts, age limits or training.

records.what_to_expect: The site shows volunteers packing toiletry bags and serving warm meals to people experiencing homelessness. It does not give shift times, how long a shift lasts or whether there is training, so ask through the form first.
records.notes: The How to Help page lists item donations (new socks, gloves, hats, scarves and toiletries), money through PayPal or a card, and an Amazon wishlist. No volunteer shifts, days or training are published. The home page says to check back for events, and the events page returned 404. The only date on the pages read is the 2026 copyright footer. The contact page publishes no email or phone number.

records.name: Make the Distinction
records.summary: A nonprofit that builds personal and professional skills in girls ages 11 to 17 so they can lead in their communities. Its leadership program takes sign-ups through a link on the programs page.
records.what_you_do: Girls take part in the group's leadership and personal development programs, such as the Leaders of Distinction program. The group also runs trips and retreats, some by invitation only.

first_step.how: Register for the Leaders of Distinction program with the REGISTER HERE link on the programs page. The page lists 10/8 (October 8) as the deadline. For questions, email contact@makethedistinction.org.
first_step.basis: The only way in is a registration form with a deadline, and the page does not say what the program involves, who is accepted or what it costs.

records.notes: The registration deadline on the programs page is 10/8, which is today's date, so this record needs a refresh once the deadline passes. The events page lists 2026 items that are invitation only (a parents night and a Mother's Day event), so they are not recorded as ways in. The In-School Program is a weekly eight-week small-group program for middle and high school students with no sign-up path shown; it is described here only. The contact page also links mtdistinction@gmail.com. The KB Foundation trip is a partner initiative and is listed under leads_only. No cost, meeting place or schedule for the Leaders of Distinction program is stated.
